name: Make missing-baseline state recovery safely actionable from the dashboard

current_round.prompt: Implement a dashboard recovery workflow for the exceptional project state-synchronization condition where the persisted three-way baseline is missing while both non-bootstrap live state and origin/refine/state exist. Reuse the existing daemon-backed GET /api/project/state-recovery/preview and POST /api/project/state-recovery/apply endpoints, including the complete-preview stale fence. Present the target and remote identities and heads, bounded conflict details, live-only/remote-only/differing/equal counts, and clear consequences of choosing live or remote authority. Never infer, recommend, or preselect authority. Require deliberate confirmation before apply. Keep browser code thin: all Git and state mutations must remain daemon-owned, and the existing fail-closed startup and synchronization behavior must not be weakened. Preserve and display the resulting audit ref, recovery manifest, published/baseline heads, and other recovery evidence. Treat Git-busy and stale-preview HTTP 409 responses as recoverable conditions with explicit refresh and retry actions that require a fresh preview and confirmation as appropriate. After a successful apply, refresh state-sync health and show that the error cleared together with the resulting heads and evidence. Add focused web and API regression coverage for preview rendering, deliberate confirmation, busy and stale rejection, successful recovery, and health-error clearing. Update affected intent or runbook documentation only where this dashboard/API surface contract changes.

- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.

findings.description: The plan does not define a daemon-owned, machine-readable signal that the failed state-sync health is specifically the missing-baseline recovery topology; the current dashboard health exposes only status and redacted error text, while calling preview for every degraded state performs remote Git inspection and changes ordinary failure behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add and test a typed recovery-eligibility or failure-kind contract from the daemon, and fetch the preview only for that condition without browser message parsing.

findings.description: The plan promises distinct busy and stale handling, but the existing API maps both conditions and other recovery conflicts to the same 409 code `conflict`, leaving a thin browser no stable way to choose the required refresh-versus-retry flow.
findings.recommendation: Define, document, and test structured recovery conflict reasons for Git-busy and stale-preview responses, then bind each UI action to that typed reason and invalidate confirmation whenever a fresh preview is required.

result.summary: Revise the plan to expose stable recovery eligibility and conflict classifications before implementing the dashboard flow.

checklist.description: Represent the missing-baseline topology as a dedicated daemon domain failure and persist an optional typed recovery kind in state-sync health so ordinary failed, stale, detached, bootstrap, and ineligible states remain distinguishable without parsing error text.

Introduce daemon-owned state-recovery conflict classifications that serialize apply-time HTTP 409 responses with stable git_busy and stale_preview reasons while leaving unrelated conflicts safely generic.

Extend the Dashboard health controller to request and retain a recovery preview only when authoritative health reports the missing-baseline recovery kind, and clear recovery state when the app, node, route context, eligibility, or preview identity changes.

Render the complete preview's target and repository identities, configured remote, local and remote heads, evidence and snapshot identifiers, live-only, remote-only, differing, and equal counts, bounded conflicting paths and truncation count, and neutral plain-language consequences of live and remote authority.

Provide initially unselected live and remote authority controls plus a separate deliberate confirmation bound to the exact displayed preview, enabling apply only after both actions and resetting confirmation whenever reviewed evidence or context changes.

Post only the explicit authority and unchanged complete preview to the existing apply route, treating git_busy as an explicit retry state that retains the preview but requires renewed confirmation and treating stale_preview as an explicit refresh state that discards the preview, authority, and confirmation before another apply.

After a successful daemon apply, settle and refetch authoritative state-sync health, preserve the success panel across that refresh, and display the cleared error, baseline creation, resulting published and local heads, recovery audit ref, manifest path, evidence identity, counts, authority, and returned detail.

Add focused daemon, API, and browser regressions for typed eligibility, eligible-only preview fetching, complete preview rendering, neutral authority controls, deliberate confirmation and invalidation, typed busy retry, stale refresh fencing, successful evidence retention, and post-apply health-error clearing without mutation on rejected requests.

Update only the Dashboard and API intent pages and the existing missing-baseline runbook section for the typed eligibility and conflict contracts, explicit authority boundary, refresh and retry semantics, and retained recovery evidence.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P1 makes missing-baseline recovery a daemon-owned typed health condition, P3 gates preview inspection on that condition, and P8 covers the eligibility contract and eligible-only fetch behavior.
P2 defines stable git_busy and stale_preview 409 reasons, P6 binds each reason to safe retry or mandatory refresh behavior with confirmation invalidation, and P8-P9 cover and document the contract.

findings.description: The plan does not define a daemon-owned, machine-readable signal that the failed state-sync health is specifically the missing-baseline recovery topology; the current dashboard health exposes only status and redacted error text, while calling preview for every degraded state performs remote Git inspection and changes ordinary failure behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add and test a typed recovery-eligibility or failure-kind contract from the daemon, and fetch the preview only for that condition without browser message parsing.

findings.description: The plan promises distinct busy and stale handling, but the existing API maps both conditions and other recovery conflicts to the same 409 code `conflict`, leaving a thin browser no stable way to choose the required refresh-versus-retry flow.
findings.recommendation: Define, document, and test structured recovery conflict reasons for Git-busy and stale-preview responses, then bind each UI action to that typed reason and invalidate confirmation whenever a fresh preview is required.

result.summary: Revise the plan to expose stable recovery eligibility and conflict classifications before implementing the dashboard flow.

checklist.description: Represent the missing-baseline topology as a dedicated daemon domain failure and persist an optional typed recovery kind in state-sync health so ordinary failed, stale, detached, bootstrap, and ineligible states remain distinguishable without parsing error text.

Introduce daemon-owned state-recovery conflict classifications that serialize apply-time HTTP 409 responses with stable git_busy and stale_preview reasons while leaving unrelated conflicts safely generic.

Extend the Dashboard health controller to request and retain a recovery preview only when authoritative health reports the missing-baseline recovery kind, and clear recovery state when the app, node, route context, eligibility, or preview identity changes.

Render the complete preview's target and repository identities, configured remote, local and remote heads, evidence and snapshot identifiers, live-only, remote-only, differing, and equal counts, bounded conflicting paths and truncation count, and neutral plain-language consequences of live and remote authority.

Provide initially unselected live and remote authority controls plus a separate deliberate confirmation bound to the exact displayed preview, enabling apply only after both actions and resetting confirmation whenever reviewed evidence or context changes.

Post only the explicit authority and unchanged complete preview to the existing apply route, treating git_busy as an explicit retry state that retains the preview but requires renewed confirmation and treating stale_preview as an explicit refresh state that discards the preview, authority, and confirmation before another apply.

After a successful daemon apply, settle and refetch authoritative state-sync health, preserve the success panel across that refresh, and display the cleared error, baseline creation, resulting published and local heads, recovery audit ref, manifest path, evidence identity, counts, authority, and returned detail.

Add focused daemon, API, and browser regressions for typed eligibility, eligible-only preview fetching, complete preview rendering, neutral authority controls, deliberate confirmation and invalidation, typed busy retry, stale refresh fencing, successful evidence retention, and post-apply health-error clearing without mutation on rejected requests.

Update only the Dashboard and API intent pages and the existing missing-baseline runbook section for the typed eligibility and conflict contracts, explicit authority boundary, refresh and retry semantics, and retained recovery evidence.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P1 makes missing-baseline recovery a daemon-owned typed health condition, P3 gates preview inspection on that condition, and P8 covers the eligibility contract and eligible-only fetch behavior.
P2 defines stable git_busy and stale_preview 409 reasons, P6 binds each reason to safe retry or mandatory refresh behavior with confirmation invalidation, and P8-P9 cover and document the contract.

result.summary: Make the exceptional missing-baseline condition safely actionable from the Dashboard by exposing daemon-owned recovery eligibility and conflict reasons, then adding a neutral preview-and-confirm flow that never chooses authority for the user, preserves the complete stale-fenced evidence, and shows authoritative health clearing and audit results after recovery without weakening ordinary fail-closed synchronization.
